title: Deprecated, Not Removed: Roots, Sampling, and Logging

questions.question: Under the MCP feature lifecycle, what does Deprecated mean for roots, sampling, and logging in the 2026-07-28 revision?
options: They were renamed but otherwise work exactly as before
They keep working fully now and face removal much later
They turned into optional extensions instead of core features
They were deleted from the schema when this revision shipped
questions.explanation: Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy means a feature stays fully specified and functional, with a migration path and at least a twelve month window before it is even eligible for removal.

questions.question: A server needs a client side language model generation while still handling a tools/call request. How does 2026-07-28 let it ask?
options: It waits for the client to poll a background task
It pushes a createMessage request to the client mid call
It returns input_required with a createMessage entry to answer
It opens a second connection and queries a model directly
questions.explanation: Sampling still exists as a deprecated client feature, and a server requests it through the multi round-trip pattern: an input_required result whose inputRequests map carries a sampling createMessage entry for the client to answer.

questions.question: A client declares no roots capability and no sampling capability on a request. What must a server needing both do?
options: Send the requests anyway since defaults cover every client
Fall back to the removed initialize handshake instead
Assume the client meant to declare both capabilities
Skip those input requests or refuse the call outright
questions.explanation: A server must not rely on a capability the caller did not declare on that request, so it can only omit the undeclared input requests or refuse the call, never assume or silently send them anyway.

questions.question: When may a server send a notifications/message notification for a given request under 2026-07-28?
options: Only when that request itself carries a logLevel in its meta
Whenever the server declares the logging capability at all
Only after the client calls the removed logging setLevel method
On the shared subscriptions listen stream once logging starts
questions.explanation: Logging now travels per request: a server may send notifications/message only on the response stream of a request whose meta carried io.modelcontextprotocol logLevel, and it must stay silent when that key is absent.

questions.question: Which of these is actually gone from the wire in 2026-07-28, rather than merely deprecated?
options: roots/list sent as an MRTR input request
logging/setLevel, the old session wide log level setter
A per-request logLevel key paired with notifications/message
sampling/createMessage sent as an MRTR input request
questions.explanation: Roots and sampling still travel as MRTR input requests and a per-request logLevel still triggers notifications/message, but logging/setLevel depended on a connection wide session that the stateless core removed outright.

questions.question: Roots was marked Deprecated in the specification revision released 2026-07-28. What is its earliest possible removal?
options: Immediately, in whichever revision ships next after this one
Never, because deprecated features stay forever by policy
The first revision released on or after 2027-07-28
Exactly 2027-07-28, regardless of when a revision actually ships
questions.explanation: The minimum deprecation window is twelve months measured from this revision's release, so the earliest removal is the first specification revision that ships as Current on or after 2027-07-28, not a fixed calendar date.
